paper_metadata.title: Design strategy for high-entropy alloys with enhanced microstructural stability and mechanical properties for high-temperature applications

evidence.quote: The use of AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy as high-temperature structural materials is limited because of their phase instability.
To address this, we designed Co-free Al – Cr – Fe – Ni alloys with spinodal structures composed of disordered body-centered cubic (BCC) (A2) and ordered BCC (B2) phases.
Finally, Al 13.6 Cr (x) Fe (75.2-x) Ni 11.2 alloys were designed and investigated for their phase stability and mechanical properties at both ambient and elevated temperatures.

Master alloy buttons (10 g), with nominal compositions of AlCoCr - FeNi, AlCrFeMnNi, AlCrFeNi and AlCrMnNi (in molar ratios), were prepared by arc-melting high-purity ( > 99.9 at%) constituent metals in an argon atmosphere. Each alloy button was re-melted five times to achieve chemical homogeneity.
Cylindrical samples with a diameter of 5 mm and height of 50 mm were fabricated by suction casting.
The as-cast ingots were then subjected to a homogenizing heat treatment at 1573 K for 6 h.

Master alloy buttons (300 g), with the nominal compositions of AlCoCrFeNi, AlCr - FeNi and Al 13.6 Cr (x) Fe (75.2-x) Ni 11.2 (x = 13.3, 21.3, 29.3 and 40.3, in at %), were prepared by plasma arc melting (PAM) the high-purity ( > 99.9 at%) constituent metals in an argon atmosphere. Each alloy button was re-melted four times to improve chemical homogeneity. A 220-mm- long, 40-mm-wide, and 20-mm-high bar-type ingots weighing 1.2 kg were fabricated using the master alloy buttons.
The as-cast ingots were then subjected to a homogenizing heat treatment at 1573 K for 6 h.
